about: Answer key for 18 fictional Common App applications (app-1.json to app-18.json) made for testing a consistency checker. All students, schools, emails and personal stories are invented; cities, colleges, programs, awards and organizations are real. High school names are made up and are not listed in publicNames. publicNames gives each real name in its full form; the text may use a shorter form (for example 'NSDA', 'Pitt' or 'the Skiway'). Brand names are included; cities and car models are not. 'mistakes' are planted inconsistencies or factual slips, either between two sections or between one section and real-world facts (kind 'wrong-city', where a single place is given). 'trickyConsistent' items look like contradictions but are both true, so a good checker should not flag them. Applications app-4, app-11 and app-16 have no planted mistakes. Quotes are copied word for word from the section's text. For numeric or list fields (hoursPerWeek, grades, level, plans) the quote is written as 'field: value', for example 'hoursPerWeek: 12' or 'grades: [10, 11, 12]'.

places.quote: hoursPerWeek: 12
I work twenty hours a week there, even during the school year

mistakes.explanation: The shop job is listed at 12 hours a week all year, but the essay says twenty hours a week even during the school year.

places.quote: Lead 9-student mech subteam
I led our twelve-person mechanical subteam

mistakes.explanation: The size of the mechanical subteam he leads is 9 in the activity list and twelve in the Georgia Tech supplement.

places.quote: hoursPerWeek: 15
During build season we're in the lab thirty-plus hours a week

trickyConsistent.explanation: Not a mistake: 15 hours is the average over a 30-week year, and the thirty-plus figure is only the few weeks of FRC build season.

places.quote: Minnesota Envirothon, 2nd Place Team
Junior year, when our team won the state competition

mistakes.explanation: The honors list says her team took 2nd at the Minnesota Envirothon in 11th grade, but the essay says the team won state junior year.

places.quote: Middlebury is a place where I can be outside and serious about science at the same time.

mistakes.explanation: The Dartmouth supplement ends by naming Middlebury, a sign it was pasted from another school's essay.

places.quote: plans: Will not continue
I'm hoping to keep racing on Nordic skis, even at the club level

mistakes.explanation: Nordic skiing is marked as not continuing in college, but the supplement says she hopes to keep racing, even at the club level.

places.quote: I didn't join debate until the spring of sophomore year

mistakes.explanation: Debate is listed for grades 9 through 12, but the essay says he didn't join until the spring of 10th grade.

places.quote: In debate, you don't get to choose which side you're on. You find out twenty minutes before the round, and then you have to argue it like you believed it your whole life.
In debate, you don't get to choose which side you're on. You find out twenty minutes before the round, and then you have to argue it like you believed it your whole life.

mistakes.explanation: The same two sentences appear word for word in the personal essay and the Johns Hopkins supplement.

places.quote: Won 1st place in Disease Detectives at the Central Jersey regional
Science Olympiad New Jersey State Tournament, 3rd Place, Disease Detectives

trickyConsistent.explanation: Not a mistake: 1st place was at the regional tournament and 3rd place was at the state tournament, which are two different competitions.

places.quote: Priyu, kaal kudu.

trickyConsistent.explanation: Not a mistake: 'Priyu' is her grandmother's affectionate nickname for Priya (the name in personalInfo), not a different name.

places.quote: IHSAA State Wrestling Tournament, 4th Place (152 lb)
Junior year I took fifth at state

mistakes.explanation: The honors list says he placed 4th at the state wrestling tournament in 11th grade, but the essay says he took fifth at state junior year (and names a calf 'Fifth Place').

places.quote: at the National FFA Convention in Louisville my junior year

mistakes.explanation: When he was a junior (fall 2025), the National FFA Convention was held in Indianapolis, as it has been every year since 2016. It was last in Louisville in 2015.

places.quote: 4th Place (152 lb)
This season I'm moving up to 160

trickyConsistent.explanation: Not a mistake: 152 lb was his junior-year weight class, and the essay says he is moving up to 160 for senior season.

places.quote: Coach 14 keiki paddlers ages 8-12
All twelve of my keiki are completely different

mistakes.explanation: The activity says she coaches 14 keiki, but the essay says twelve.

places.quote: Hawaiʻi State Science and Engineering Fair, 2nd Place, Plant Sciences
That project won first place at the state science fair

mistakes.explanation: The honors list says 2nd place at the state science fair, but the UW supplement says the same project won first place.

places.quote: Called cues for 3 mainstage shows
grades: [11, 12]
Across the eleven shows I've stage-managed since freshman year

mistakes.explanation: The activity says Rowan has stage-managed 3 mainstage shows, in grades 11 and 12 only. The essay says eleven shows since freshman year, and elsewhere in the essay Rowan says they only asked to join crew after the summer following sophomore year.

places.quote: the Oregon Shakespeare Festival in Portland

mistakes.explanation: The Oregon Shakespeare Festival is in Ashland, Oregon, not Portland.

places.quote: placed 3rd at state in 2026
Michigan HOSA State Leadership Conference, 1st Place, Medical Terminology

mistakes.explanation: The HOSA activity says she placed 3rd at state in Medical Terminology in 2026, but the honors list says 1st place at the same state conference in 11th grade.

places.quote: hoursPerWeek: 4
I volunteer there every Saturday for three years now, six hours at a time

mistakes.explanation: ACCESS tutoring is listed at 4 hours a week, but the essay says six hours every Saturday.

places.quote: Al-Sayed Family Bakery
my uncle's bakery on Warren Avenue

trickyConsistent.explanation: Not a mistake: the 'family bakery' belongs to her uncle, who shares the Al-Sayed name, so 'family bakery' and 'my uncle's bakery' describe the same job.

places.quote: level: National
Last year I won a regional computing award

mistakes.explanation: The NCWIT honor is an affiliate (New Mexico) award and the supplement calls it a regional award, but the honors list gives its level as National instead of State/Regional.

places.quote: So I started our school's Girls Who Code club last fall.

mistakes.explanation: The essay was written in fall of senior year, so 'last fall' means 11th grade. But the club she founded is listed as starting in 10th grade.

places.quote: 16 members build web apps
our nine members

mistakes.explanation: The activity says the Girls Who Code club has 16 members, but the Yale supplement says nine.

places.quote: hoursPerWeek: 6
spend the rest of the day with the sheep, from sunrise until it gets dark

trickyConsistent.explanation: Not a mistake: the 6 hours a week is an average over the whole year ('Weekends and summers'), and the essay is describing full summer days at her grandmother's place.

places.quote: competing at Nationals at Georgetown in D.C.

mistakes.explanation: The National History Day National Contest is held at the University of Maryland in College Park, not at Georgetown in Washington, D.C.

places.quote: I've played hockey since I was five

trickyConsistent.explanation: Not a mistake: the activity is the school varsity team (grades 10-12), and the essay is about playing hockey in general since childhood.

places.quote: Interviewed 6 Boston residents on camera.
I interviewed six people

trickyConsistent.explanation: Not a mistake: the essay's six interviews don't include Uncle Frank, whose interview he chose not to use, so the count of six matches the activity.

places.quote: level: State/Regional
It went to nationals and didn't place

trickyConsistent.explanation: Not a mistake: Scholastic Gold Keys are regional awards, and Gold Key work moves on to national judging. Her piece was judged nationally but didn't win there, so State/Regional is the right level.

places.quote: hoursPerWeek: 10
hoursPerWeek: 12

trickyConsistent.explanation: Not a mistake: these are two different swim programs, the high school team and a year-round YMCA club, so their hours are separate and both can be true.

places.quote: Editor-in-Chief (12); News Editor (11)
Last year, as news editor of our school paper

trickyConsistent.explanation: Not a mistake: she was news editor in 11th grade, when she wrote the red tide piece, and is editor-in-chief now.

places.quote: State champion, Entrepreneurship Series
Georgia DECA State Career Development Conference, 2nd Place, Entrepreneurship Series

mistakes.explanation: The DECA activity calls him state champion in the Entrepreneurship Series, but the honors list says 2nd place at the same state conference.

places.quote: hoursPerWeek: 15
with the 25 hours a week I work

mistakes.explanation: The Chick-fil-A job is listed at 15 hours a week, but the Vanderbilt supplement says 25 hours a week.

places.quote: I flew to New York for the Student Leaders Summit

mistakes.explanation: The Bank of America Student Leaders Summit is held in Washington, D.C., not New York.

places.quote: Concertmaster of the Symphony Orchestra, HYS's top ensemble.
This year, as principal second violin in Houston Youth Symphony

mistakes.explanation: The activity lists her as concertmaster of Houston Youth Symphony in 11th and 12th grade, but the essay says that this year she is principal second violin. Those are different chairs.

places.quote: grades: [10, 11]
I made All-State for the first time junior year.

mistakes.explanation: All-State is listed for 10th and 11th grade, but the essay says she missed it as a sophomore and made it for the first time junior year.

places.quote: That balance is what I'd find at Rice, and it's why I think I would thrive there.

mistakes.explanation: The Duke supplement names Rice in its last sentence.

places.quote: Used by 1,200 students in my district.
About 300 people use BusBuddy now

mistakes.explanation: The activity says 1,200 students use BusBuddy, but the essay says about 300 people do.

places.quote: I got my first job at Giant Eagle the summer after junior year
grades: [11]

mistakes.explanation: The Giant Eagle job is listed for grades 10 through 12, but the essay says it was his first job and started the summer after junior year. The essay's date also breaks the app timeline: he says he started tracking the bus on the way to that job, yet the app won the Congressional App Challenge in 11th grade. 'Summer after sophomore year' would make everything fit.

places.quote: the Iowa Young Writers' Studio in Ames

mistakes.explanation: The Iowa Young Writers' Studio is run by the University of Iowa in Iowa City, not in Ames (home of Iowa State).

places.quote: Co-lead a 28-person staff with one other editor.
As the paper's first solo editor-in-chief

mistakes.explanation: The activity says she shares the top job as co-editor-in-chief, but the essay calls her the paper's first solo editor-in-chief.

places.quote: Joined in Colorado Springs; moved to an Anchorage squadron midway through 10th grade.
I joined as a freshman in Colorado Springs

trickyConsistent.explanation: Not a mistake: his current school is in Anchorage, but CAP is a national organization and he joined in Colorado Springs in 9th grade before his family moved. Grades 9-12 in one CAP activity across two states is correct.

places.quote: grades: [10]
in the fall of my sophomore year I earned the Billy Mitchell Award

trickyConsistent.explanation: Not a mistake: he earned the Mitchell Award in 10th grade in Colorado, two months before moving to Alaska midway through 10th grade, so the award and the move both fit grade 10.

places.quote: I've moved five times since kindergarten
I've lived in six states

trickyConsistent.explanation: Not a mistake: five moves starting from Ohio (Ohio to Texas, Georgia, Virginia, Colorado, Alaska) means six states lived in. The essay's box has also 'been to six states'.

places.quote: 6-week residential number theory program.
Last summer, I spent eight weeks at the Ross Mathematics Program at Ohio State.

mistakes.explanation: The activity calls Ross a 6-week program (which it is), but the essay says he spent eight weeks there.

places.quote: Starting center back and captain for 2 seasons.
As a striker, I'm always calculating angles and spaces

mistakes.explanation: The activity lists him as a center back, a defender, but the essay describes him as a striker.

places.quote: I want to study mathematics, specifically number theory, and I want to understand how pure math connects to the real world.

mistakes.explanation: The WashU supplement has a 200-word limit, but the text runs well over 200 words.

places.quote: Ross Mathematics Program, The Ohio State University
The weirdest part was that Ross was twenty minutes from my house.

trickyConsistent.explanation: Not a mistake: he lives in Columbus, where Ohio State is, so a residential program twenty minutes from home is correct. Ross is residential even for local students.

places.quote: South Carolina ProStart Invitational, 2nd Place, Culinary
after our team won state at the ProStart Invitational

mistakes.explanation: The honors list says the team took 2nd place at the South Carolina ProStart Invitational, but the Cornell supplement says they won state.

places.quote: Lead our 4-person culinary team
the five of us practiced every afternoon for months
Dre was our alternate, so he didn't get to cook that day

trickyConsistent.explanation: Not a mistake: four people cook in a ProStart culinary team, and the fifth practice member, Dre, was the alternate. Both counts are true.
